title: Catalog onboarding concierge playbook
content:
Purpose:
This is a working playbook to support a concierge-style onboarding for partners listing in cloud marketplaces (AWS/GCP/Azure). Goal is to reduce back-and-forth, shorten time-to-publish to 7–10 business days for qualified partners, and capture consistent copy + technical artifacts for legal/ops review.

Scope:
- Applies to partners who need a managed onboarding (partner-facing PM + GTM engineer).
- Covers listing creative (tile & long description), technical gating (SSO, billing, KMS, data residency), and launch checklist.
- Not a replacement for the full marketplace guide — this is a condensed, task-oriented concierge flow.

How to use this doc:
- GTM lead runs the checklist during kickoff.
- Engineering/solutions uses the technical gating section.
- Legal/Security sign off on assets flagged in the risk matrix.

Quick TL;DR checklist (concierge run):
1) Intake call scheduled (PM + partner + infra eng) – owner: GTM lead
2) Asset deposit (tile image, logo, support URL, contact) – owner: partner
3) Technical vet (billing SKU mapping, entitlement test) – owner: GTM engineer
4) Security review (KMS/keys, data residency attestation) – owner: Security reviewer
5) Final copy freeze and marketplace submission – owner: GTM lead
6) Smoke test post-publish (1hr, 24hr, 7d) – owner: Solutions eng

Required partner deliverables (initial intake):
- High-res tile image (1200x627 recommended) + logo SVG (transparent)
- One-sentence product tagline (<= 12 words) and 200–400 word description
- Support doc URL, SLA summary, and sales contact email
- Billing entity details, legal contact, and representative for contract questions

Marketplace copy templates (pick & adapt)
- Hero tagline (short, conversion-focused):
  Option A: "Deploy inference at scale — predictable latency, lower unit cost."
  Option B: "Enterprise LLM inference with predictable performance and flexible deployment."
- 25–40 word tile blurb (uses for catalog lists):
  "Redwood Inference provides production-grade LLM serving with hosted, dedicated, and private deployments — built for teams that need predictable latency and clear unit economics."
- 200–400 word long description (structure):
  1) Lead-in (what problem it solves) 2) Key features (hosted API, Dedicated, Private, Console) 3) Benefits (SLA, cost controls, rollout safety) 4) Getting started + links to docs

Creative/asset checklist
- Tile image: 1200x627 PNG or JPG, <2MB, no crowded text
- Logo: SVG + PNG fallback, transparent background
- Screenshots: annotated, captions describing UI or telemetry (max 3)
- Video (optional): 30–60s demo clip, MP4, hosted URL

Technical gating (minimums for concierge accept):
- Authentication: partner must provide owner contact & support SAML/OIDC for private deployments (if requested).
- Billing: confirmed SKU mapping + pricing tier (documented in submission sheet).
- Telemetry: event name map for usage telemetry (catalog must show sample call and test token).
- Entitlements: verified test user that can exercise the listing flow (sandbox account or demo keys).
- Data residency: partner statement of where customer data is stored and retention policy.
- Encryption & keys: KMS provider used for private installations; HSM required for certain regulated customers (flag with security).

Acceptance checklist (concierge sign-off) — mark Y/N and owner initials:
- [ ] Tile + logo accepted
- [ ] Copy final and legal-approved
- [ ] Billing & SKU mapping validated
- [ ] Sandbox entitlement tests pass
- [ ] Security sign-off on KMS/residency
- [ ] Support contact & runbook uploaded
- [ ] Screenshots/video approved

Rollout timeline (example 8-day concierge lane)
Day 0: Intake + asset list
Day 1: GTM lead triage + partner delivers assets
Day 2: Engineering runs SKU mapping + creates sandbox test users
Day 3: Security does KMS/residency review
Day 4: Draft copy -> legal review
Day 5: Final assets uploaded, marketplace submission initiated
Day 6–7: Marketplace review (external)
Day 8: Publish smoke test + quick PR to announce

Risk matrix (quick callouts)
- KMS mismatch: high risk — requires Security escalation and may block private deployment listings.
- Unsupported billing model (metered non-standard): medium risk — may need custom integration or co-bill solution.
- Data residency conflict: high risk — requires legal + infra remediation.
- Misleading claims in copy: high risk — legal rewrite and partner coaching.

Common gotchas & patterns we see:
- Partners submit long, feature-dense descriptions that reduce conversion — recommend 2–3 benefits first.
- Tile images with small text get rejected by marketplace automated checks — keep imagery clean.
- Metering differences across clouds require explicit SKUs per cloud — document early.

Communication templates (short snippets)
- Asset request (to partner):
  "Thanks — please upload your tile (1200x627), logo SVG, 1-line tagline, and 200–400 word description to the shared intake folder by EOD Wed. We’ll do an initial triage and follow up with technical requests."
- Post-publish smoke test note (internal):
  "Publish complete for <partner-name>. Smoke tests: 1hr ok, 24hr latency median 120ms, errors 0.3%. See telemetry dashboard: <link>."

Unresolved questions / next decisions:
- Should we require partners to provide a privacy/processing addendum for Private deployments? (Legal)
- Do we standardize on one sample telemetry event map per product category? (Telemetry owner)
- Who owns marketplace SKUs for multi-region pricing adjustments? (GTM vs Finance)

Next steps (action items):
- Assign concierge owner for next three inbound partners — @Ethan Brooks (GTM)
- Create a shared intake Drive folder template with required fields — owner: Priya
- Draft a short landing page snippet for partners that want self-serve listing (minimal bundle) — owner: Maya

- Company name:
- Product short name (<= 30 chars):
- Tagline (<= 12 words):
- 200–400 word description:
- Tile image URL:
- Logo URL:
- Support URL:
- Billing entity + SKU mapping:
- Sandbox test user credentials:
- Data residency statement (region + retention):
- KMS provider and key id (if applicable):

Notes to self: keep this doc lean. If concierge becomes the norm, we should bake the checklist into a tiny app for intake and auto-mapping to the marketplace submission fields.
